result.stdout:
Usage: roblox-cs [<input>...] [options]
       roblox-cs init [<dir>] [--name <name>] [--template <game|experience>] [--force]
       roblox-cs add <server|client|module|class> <name> [--dir <folder>]
       roblox-cs add place <name> [--id <place id>]
       roblox-cs map <output-dir> [<script>:<line>...]
       roblox-cs instances <sourcemap.json> [-o <file.cs>] [--class <name>] [--namespace <name>]
       roblox-cs upgrade [--config <file>] [--dry-run] [--no-skills]
       roblox-cs --version

  <input>              A .cs file, a directory to search for .cs files, or a
                       .csproj project (its Compile items, LangVersion,
                       Nullable, DefineConstants and references are used).
  -o, --out <dir>      Write one .luau file per .cs file into <dir>, keeping
                       the folder layout of each input directory or project.
                       Files whose text did not change are not rewritten.
                       Without --out, the Luau code is printed to stdout.
  --rojo <file>        The Rojo project that maps the output files to Roblox
                       instances, used to compute requires between files.
                       With --out, default.project.json is used when it is
                       next to the input project or directory, or in the
                       current directory.
  --no-rojo            Do not use a Rojo project: requires are relative paths
                       that mirror the output folder layout.
  -c, --configuration <name>
                       The project configuration (default Debug), as in
                       dotnet build: selects conditions and defines DEBUG
                       or RELEASE in SDK projects.
  -p:<name>=<value>    Set a project property (also --property:<name>=<value>).
  -d, --define <name>  Define a preprocessor symbol for every file.
  --source-maps        Write <file>.luau.map next to each output, mapping its
                       lines to the C# lines (see 'roblox-cs map').
  --strict          
[truncated]
